sentences.text: Bacteria of the genus Pseudomonas are described as omnipresent in air, soil and water, and have been widely studied for their broad metabolic versatility.
A comparative genomic study of 3,274 genomes from strains isolated in diverse environments detected functional divergence of Pseudomonas that depended on the niche occupied.
Those niches include living hosts such as animals and plants, according to the same study.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is considered one of the most important lung pathogens in people with cystic fibrosis, a disease marked by recurring bacterial infections.

A systematic review reported chronic P. aeruginosa detection falling from 51.4 percent at baseline to 24.8 percent after elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor, with persistent molecular detection despite negative cultures.
